segment.description: Sequatchie Valley headwaters in Cumberland County, which TWRA spring-stocks with catchable rainbows; the river runs the full valley from the Cumberland County headwaters down toward the Tennessee River at Shellmound. The Whitwell gauge sits far downstream and is treated as a valley-level trend, not headwater truth.
segment.boundaries: Stocked segment: Cumberland County headwaters (TWRA 2026 schedule row 'Cumberland | Sequatchie River'). USGS 03571000 'SEQUATCHIE RIVER NEAR WHITWELL, TN' (35.20572, -85.49703) is on the LOWER river in Marion County — outside the stocked headwater segment.

coldSource.notes: USGS 03571000 'SEQUATCHIE RIVER NEAR WHITWELL, TN': Marion County (FIPS 115), HUC 06020004, altitude 632.42 ft, drainage 402 sq mi, free-flowing river station (https://waterservices.usgs.gov/nwis/site/?sites=03571000&siteOutput=expanded&format=rdb). Its only water-temperature record is historical daily values 1962-1971; July daily maxima at this lower-river station reached 23.9 C (Jul 1965), 25.6 C (Jul 1966) and 25.0 C (Jul 1968) (https://waterservices.usgs.gov/nwis/dv/?sites=03571000&parameterCd=00010&statCd=00001&startDT=1965-07-01&endDT=1965-07-31&format=json and same endpoint for 1966/1968).

holdover.detail: No holdover evidence located; the documented program is spring-seasonal put-and-take (rainbows, weeks of 3/22, 3/29 and 5/17/2026).

wildPopulation.detail: Sequatchie River is absent from TWRA's Wild Trout Streams list (that list covers Monroe/Carter/Johnson/Greene/Unicoi county waters only); no trout survey record found. (A federally documented fish for the river is the sickle darter, a warmwater darter, per the ESA final rule consulted in the prior project pass.)

overallSurvivalRead.oneLineWhy: Spring-seasonal rainbow stockings (Mar-May 2026) are the only trout program; the river's only temperature record (lower river near Whitwell, 1960s daily values) ran 23.5-25.6 C in July, and nothing documents headwater summer temperatures or survival.
